newsitem.title: USA: Rogers Corp acquires Bisco Products.
newsitem.headline: Rogers Corp acquires Bisco Products.

text.p: Rogers Corp said on Friday that it completed the acquisition of Bisco Products, a maker of silicone foam materials, from Dow Corning Corp, for $12 million.
Bisco's silicone products are being integrated into Rogers High Performance Elastomers Division, Rogers said.
On July 30, 1996, Rogers signed a Letter of Intent to purchase the Bisco Products business, which makes products for the electrical, transportation, printing, footwear and medical applications.

A Rogers spokeswoman said Bisco Products is not involved with the manufacture of silicon breast implants, which led Dow Corning to file for bankruptcy because of litigation related to illnesses from women who recieve implants.
Dow Corning Corp is a joint venture between Dow Chemical and Corning Inc.
